title: Onboarding reasoning smoke tests and quick pack
content:
Overview:
This is a compact, pragmatic smoke-test pack for onboarding new model checkpoints into Redwood Inference serving. Goal: catch high-impact reasoning/math regressions fast (under 2–5 minutes total run time on local harness) so engineers can triage before a full eval run. This lives in Drive as a lightweight working spec + prompt set that the applied-ml team can iterate on.

Motivation and scope:
- We frequently see subtle regressions after model swaps that only show up on short-chain numerical logic (off-by-one, unit mistakes) or when the model mode flips into verbose chain-of-thought (CoT) despite a suppression preference.
- Long eval suites are expensive. This pack is a gate: quick pass -> full regression; fail -> block, investigate.
- Focus areas: word-problem arithmetic (3–6 steps), step-constraint enforcement (explicit step limits), CoT suppression robustness, verifier-style yes/no checks for numeric claims.

Quick acceptance criteria (smoke):
- Overall accuracy >= 85% on the pack for the baseline model (used as reference).
- Any model with a drop >= 8% vs baseline triggers a triage workflow.
- CoT leakage: fewer than 5% of responses containing explicit "chain-of-thought" style markers ("I think", multi-step enumerated reasoning) when suppression prompt is applied.

Prompt templates (canonical):
1) Step-limited arithmetic (explicit constraint):
Prompt: "Solve in at most 2 steps. Show only the final numeric answer.

Q: A farmer has 14 apples and gives 5 to his neighbor, then picks 3 more from the tree. How many apples does he have now?"
Expected: "12"

2) CoT suppression test:
Prompt: "Answer briefly. Do not show your reasoning. Provide only the numeric result.

Q: If a train travels 60 miles in 1.5 hours, what is the average speed in mph?"
Expected: "40" (and response should not include step-by-step text)

3) Verifier micro-test (claim-check):
Prompt: "Claim: \"A rectangle with width 7 and length 5 has area 35.\" Is this claim correct? Answer Yes or No only."
Expected: "Yes"

Compact dataset (example composition):
- 28 total items: 12 word-problems (3-step-ish), 8 step-constraint checks, 6 verifier yes/no claims, 2 trick numerics (unit conversion / negative numbers).
- Hand-curated seed examples included below (seed IDs: S1..S28). These should be stable across runs.

Scoring rubric (smoke):
- Exact-match on numeric answer OR normalized numeric (allow 1% rounding for floats).
- For yes/no verifier, accept only exact case-insensitive "yes"/"no"; any additional text fails.
- For step-constraint tests, if response includes more text than allowed (e.g., extra steps/CoT) mark as CoT leakage failure even if numeric is correct.

Automation and quick-run notes:
- Local harness: repo/github link in linked_artifacts. Quick command: `python -m onboarding_smoke.run --model <checkpoint> --seed-pack S1-S28 --timeout 300`
- Harness outputs JSONL with fields: id, prompt, response, normalized_answer, ok(true/false), failure_reason. (This is produced by the harness; not nested here.)

Regression thresholds and alerting:
- Baseline model (tagged baseline/onboarding-ref-2025-09) accuracy annotated in CI; a regression >=8% triggers an automated label on the PR and notification to #applied-ml-alerts Slack via webhook.
- CoT leakage increases >5 percentage points vs baseline triggers immediate hold for manual review.

Example seeds (selected to be minimally redundant):
S3: "A baker had 24 cookies. He packs them into boxes of 6. How many boxes?" -> 4
S7: step-limit 1: "Solve in at most 1 step. Give only the number. Q: 9*7 - 14 = ?" -> 49
S12: verifier: "Claim: 0.5 km = 500 meters. Correct? Answer Yes or No only." -> Yes
S19: trick negative: "If you subtract -3 from 5 what is the result?" -> 8
S25: float rounding: "A tip of 18% on a $27.50 bill is how many dollars? Round to nearest cent." -> 4.95

Open questions / known gaps:
- Coverage: pack is intentionally small; we need a lightweight way to select 1–2 failing representatives to feed back into larger evals automatically.
- Locale/formatting: numeric formats with commas/periods vary by model; we should standardize normalization rules in harness.
- Prompt phrasing: some models interpret "brief" differently; consider an explicit suppression token or system prompt in future private deployments.

Next steps and immediate TODOs (owner: Jordan):
- [ ] Finalize seed list to 30 items (deadline 2026-02-10).
- [ ] Add deterministic RNG seeding to harness (PR: linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Wire CI thresholds and Slack alerts (ENG-8342).
- [ ] Add a small notebook with manual triage checklist for failures and typical fixes (e.g., enable quantization-compat variant, switch to baseline tokenizer).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight and iterative. Comments welcome on additional high-impact checks (e.g., currency conversions, unit mismatch detection).
- If you add seeds, use S## naming and append a one-line rationale for coverage.
